content.title: About
content.content: Hass avocado is a variety with a dark‑green, slightly bumpy skin that turns almost black when ripe. The fruit is large, buttery, and contains a single large seed. Peeled raw Hass avocado is commonly used in salads, smoothies, guacamole, and as a butter substitute.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The Hass cultivar was first grown in California in the 1920s and is now the world’s most popular avocado.
Avocados contain more monounsaturated fats than most fruits and vegetables.
Hass fruits continue to ripen after harvest, so they are often sold slightly firm.
The seed can be planted to grow a new avocado tree.
Avocado provides more vitamin E than most nuts.

items.title: Rich in monounsaturated fats
items.content: These fats help lower LDL cholesterol and support heart health.

items.title: High potassium content
items.content: Potassium aids blood‑pressure regulation and muscle function.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins and folate
items.content: Vitamin B6, B5 and folate are important for metabolism and nervous‑system health.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Lutein and zeaxanthin protect the eyes from age‑related degeneration.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Dietary fiber promotes regular bowel movements.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to avocado.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Avocado is calorie‑rich, so portion control is advisable for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Possible drug interactions
items.content: Large potassium amounts can affect certain medications, such as diuretics.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Eat avocado fresh, add it to salads, smoothies, toast, or use it as a base for guacamole. It can also replace butter in baking. For a smoother texture, mash the flesh with a fork.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep whole avocados in the refrigerator’s fruit drawer – they stay fresh for up to 5 days. Peeled avocado should be stored in an airtight container with a splash of lemon juice to prevent browning.
